gaps.hint: past participle after 'have'; the verb takes no object
gaps.explanation: 'Rise' (rise, rose, risen) takes no object: sales have risen. 'Raise' takes an object: they raised prices.

gaps.sentence: The consultant will ___ us on every stage of the merger.
gaps.explanation: 'Advise' is the verb; 'advice' is the noun.

gaps.sentence: The two brothers are ___ in appearance but not in character.
gaps.explanation: 'They are alike' — 'alike' follows the verb and cannot come before a noun.

gaps.sentence: My brother is six foot three — he is much ___ than me.
gaps.explanation: 'Tall' is used for people's height, so the comparative is 'taller'; 'higher' is for heights above a level.

gaps.sentence: This tooth is ___ and will probably fall out soon.
gaps.explanation: 'Loose' is an adjective meaning not firmly fixed; 'lose' is the verb meaning to no longer have.

gaps.sentence: We ___ all major credit cards at the box office.
gaps.explanation: 'Accept' means to take or agree to something offered; 'except' means not including.

gaps.sentence: Our team has a good ___ of winning on Saturday.
gaps.hint: pattern: have a good ___ of doing something
gaps.explanation: 'Have a chance of doing something' is the standard collocation for the likelihood of success.

gaps.sentence: A car remained ___ at the traffic lights for ages.
gaps.explanation: 'Stationary' means not moving; 'stationery' means pens, paper and other writing materials.
